tagline: A short run into a college village in the Welsh Hills.
intro: From SR 37 the byway takes James Road and then turns north on SR 661 into Granville, through the rural hills known locally as the Welsh Hills. Settlers from Granville, Massachusetts, came in 1805 and named the village after the town they had left, and Welsh families followed and left their names on the map.

It has long been a school town, home to Denison University since 1831, and it was once a hotbed of temperance and abolitionist activity. Greek Revival houses and St. Luke's Episcopal Church of 1837 stand along the streets.

moments.title: Buxton Inn
moments.text: Opened in 1812 as The Tavern and post office, it took Major Horton Buxton's name in 1865, and a later owner, an opera singer, lived in Room 9 with a cat called Major Buxton.

moments.title: Alligator Effigy Mound
moments.text: On a rounded spur of land above the village lies an earthen figure built about a thousand years ago, called the Alligator, though it may stand for the underwater panther of Native American myth.

moments.title: Swasey Chapel
moments.text: Its design borrows from several of Christopher Wren's London churches, and it was the first building of a grand campus plan that the Great Depression stopped after the chapel and two dormitories.
